function: Radio map prediction: KAN regresses path loss/RSRP from distance, frequency, heights and LOS (p. 4), a propagation model for network planning (p. 1), outside the seven areas.
notes: Exclusion code function (Step 1, check 5). Checks 1-4 pass: a research article that proposes and evaluates RadioKAN; the model is learned (p. 6: 'The LBFGS optimizer is used to train for 20 epochs'); its output is a propagation quantity, not a network decision. The learned task is radio map prediction: p. 4 'the path loss P (dBm) at the reception point is taken as the output'; p. 1 Index Terms 'wireless propagation model, radio map prediction'; p. 1 radio maps 'are crucial for resource allocation and network planning'. Baselines are empirical propagation models (COST-231, SPM, COST-231WI) and radio-map estimators (Table II p. 8, Table III p. 10). No symbol detection, link CSI estimation or feedback, precoder/beam/RIS design, OTFS, ISAC beam/waveform/resource design, NTN control, or over-the-air FL; ISAC appears only as motivation (p. 1). For the reviewer: if path-loss radio-map prediction were counted as large-scale channel prediction (area 2), the work would still be excluded, by code system: single-antenna links and no RIS (p. 7: '80 omnidirectional antenna base stations'; Table I p. 7: antenna type Isotropic/Directional; p. 10: 'Assume that the receiving antenna is an omnidirectional antenna'). Page 1 holds the title and DOI 10.1109/TCCN.2025.3603700, so the PDF is the paper of this DOI.
